title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The decision outlines the AI Office's stance on governance of artificial intelligence within the organization. It establishes guidelines for responsible development, deployment, and oversight of AI systems to ensure safety, fairness, and compliance with regulations.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy outlines the process for filling office vacancies with technology specialists focused on AI. It specifies the roles, responsibilities, and qualifications required for individuals who will develop and manage AI solutions in the organization.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This AI policy document announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, detailing the duties, required qualifications, and the importance of the role. It highlights the need for scientific oversight in AI research and policy, and outlines the application and selection process for candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The document explains how AI tools can be used to fill or supplement legal officer positions in the office, aiming to address staff shortages and increase efficiency. It also sets out rules for using AI in legal work, ensuring compliance, accountability, and proper oversight.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy outlines the openings for Policy Officers in the AI Office, detailing the responsibilities, qualifications, and application procedure for these positions. It explains how these officers will support the office’s AI strategy, governance, and compliance efforts.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts who evaluate the proposed AI regulations in the European Union’s AI Act to ensure they are scientifically sound and practical. Their work focuses on balancing innovation, public safety, and ethical considerations while providing guidance for lawmakers and industry stakeholders.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document proposes a formal request for the standardization of AI systems, outlining the need for consistent technical guidelines and regulatory frameworks. It also highlights the roles of stakeholders in creating and adopting these standards to ensure safety, interoperability, and public trust.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation period for establishing or updating a Community of Practice (CoP). It invites stakeholders to provide input on the scope, objectives, and operational guidelines of the CoP.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for individuals or organizations to express interest in joining a new Community of Practice (CoP) focused on advancing AI policy discussions. It outlines the purpose, benefits, and application process for those who wish to collaborate on shaping responsible AI governance.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This policy provides a visual overview of the iterative drafting process used within the Community of Practice, showing each step from initial concept to final approval. It explains how drafts are repeatedly refined through collaboration and feedback to ensure clear, effective policy outcomes.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document is a graphic that illustrates the step-by-step timeline involved in drafting a policy. It shows the sequence of stages, milestones, and key dates from the initial drafting phase through review and final approval.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The document is the first draft of a Code of Practice for AI, outlining basic principles for safe and ethical use. It offers a set of suggested rules and guidelines to help developers and users act responsibly and in line with emerging standards.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document is the second draft of a Code of Practice that establishes guidelines for responsible AI development, deployment, and governance. It aims to promote transparency, safety, fairness, and accountability by offering detailed best‑practice recommendations for all stakeholders involved in AI projects.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 3rd Draft outlines guidelines for the responsible development and deployment of AI systems. It sets out standards, compliance measures, and best practices to ensure ethical, safe, and trustworthy use of AI technologies by stakeholders.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft outlines a framework for responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence, focusing on transparency, safety, and societal benefit. It calls for collaboration among governments, industry, and civil society to set shared standards and ensure AI technologies are used ethically and securely.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that sets out how AI should be developed, used, and governed responsibly. It establishes commitments to transparency, safety, fairness, and accountability, aiming to ensure that AI technologies are deployed ethically and benefit society.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The guidelines list AI practices that are prohibited, such as creating deceptive content, violating privacy, or enabling illegal activities, to protect users from harm. They provide a clear rule set that developers and users must follow to ensure responsible and ethical use of AI.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy provides clear definitions for what constitutes an AI system, helping organizations identify when they are using AI technology. It outlines key characteristics, scope, and examples to guide compliance and risk assessment.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This document outlines strategies for fostering start‑ups and promoting innovation through targeted communication efforts. It discusses how clear messaging, stakeholder engagement, and supportive policies can help create a more vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is designed to help early-stage companies gain access to high‑performance computing resources and expertise across Europe. By providing infrastructure, funding, and collaborative opportunities with leading HPC centers, it aims to accelerate innovation and growth in computing‑intensive industries.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy outlines a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It defines responsibilities and monitoring processes to ensure safe, responsible deployment of AI technologies.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy document is a video webinar titled “Risk Management” that focuses on identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks associated with the development and deployment of AI systems. It provides guidance on best practices for risk assessment, monitoring, and response strategies to ensure responsible AI use.
